target_claim: Running the specified Dijkstra variant (min-key with reinsertion on strict decrease) on the explicitly constructed DAG family G_n from source a0 performs at least 2^n RELAX invocations (via the intermediate claim T_n >= 2^n extractions of a_n).
source_quote:
0087 | |V (Gn)| = 2n + 2) such that running Dijkstra’s min-key algorithm (with reinsertions on
0088 | decreases) on Gn from source a0 performs at least 2n invocations of RELAX.
test_sketch: Implement the fully specified graph family (vertices a_0..a_n, b_1..b_n, t; edges a_{i-1}->a_i weight 0, a_{i-1}->b_i weight W_i=B^{n-i} with B=4n+5, b_i->a_i weight -W_i-1, a_n->t weight 0) and the specified min-key Dijkstra with reinsertion on strict decrease (~50 lines Python). Instrument a counter incremented on every edge scan (RELAX invocation) and a per-vertex extraction counter. Run for n=1..8. Measured: total RELAX count is (n+1)(3n/2+1) - quadratic - giving 92 < 2^7 = 128 at n=7 and 117 < 256 at n=8, refuting the >= 2^n claim; moreover extractions of a_n equal n+1, refuting the intermediate claim 'Tn >= 2^n T0 = 2^n' (line 0079) already at n=2 (3 < 4). Root cause: in an i-epoch the direct edge a_{i-1}->a_i yields no strict decrease (d[a_i] was already lowered to the same value by the in-epoch b_i cascade), so the two-extractions-per-epoch lemma fails; the solution's own invariant -d[a_j] <= n caps each a_j at n+1 extractions, making the count polynomial regardless of tie-breaking. Confirmed by actual simulation.
